extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners, KIPO staff, and patent applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Official Korean Patent Office (KIPO) procedural guidelines for examining patent applications, covering formal requirement checks, classification assignment (IPC/CPC), treatment of amendments, reexamination, examiner duties, reporting, and confidentiality. Intended to guide examiners and inform applicants/agents of procedural rules and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple written amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters to be amended in the concerned written amendments shall be determined by combining the written amendment submitted before with the final amendments by matters to be amended. As to the patent application filed on and after July 1, 2013, any other amendments submitted before the last amendment shall be deemed to have been withdrawn; refusal to enter the amendment shall be determined based on the last filed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed methods referred to Part V, Chapter 3, Section 6.3 Treatment of Amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding effect of appeal revocation on examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a decision to reject has been revoked according to Article 176(1) and (2) and the application has been remanded to an examination bureau, the reason which leads to revocation of the decision shall be binding upon the examiner pursuant to Paragraph (3) of the same article (the disposition of an appeal decision and the findings of fact which form the premise of the decision) in the examination of the remanded patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the decision to reject or to refuse to enter an amendment is revoked; earlier proceedings remain effective and the remanded application shall be examined normally. Where examiner notifies rejection necessitated by amendment made in response to prior rejection, the rejection shall be non-final taking into account hardship to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendment after appeal reversal and new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision to refuse to enter an amendment is revoked in appeal but new grounds for refusal (not mentioned in the decision and not reviewed during appeal) are found, the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment based on the new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, regarding illegitimate amendments made before an appeal request under Article 170, the examiner shall not refuse to enter the amendment but shall examine the amendment considering prohibition of refusal to enter and possibilities of unexpected damage to applicant if refused by citing previously overlooked grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments filed shortly before appeal (pre-2009 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent applications filed before June 30, 2009 and which underwent reconsideration by an examiner before a trial and were revoked and returned, an amendment made thirty days before the filing date of an appeal against a decision to reject shall not be declined at the examination stage since Article 51 only applies to an amendment under Article 47(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, even where a new ground to refuse to enter an amendment is found, an examiner shall not refuse to enter an amendment again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of formal requirements checks whether an application meets formal requirements: capacity, representation, formality requirements of the application, fees, and provisions on returning application documents per Article 11(1) of the Enforcement Rules of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary check is in principle carried out by the receiving office in the name of the Commissioner of KIPO; if the receiving office fails, an examiner may conduct further checks in the Commissioner's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of patent classification (CPC, IPC) based on claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification of a patent application is assigned taking into consideration the invention as claimed. Classification is necessary as an effective search tool for retrieval of patent documents by IP offices and other users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO adopts the IPC; CPC allocation is used for search; pre-classification and confirmation processes apply (see flowchart). Examiner must review pre-classification before examination and request corrections if inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open (publication) timing and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be laid open in the Patent Gazette as soon as after the expiration of eighteen months from the date of filing (or earliest priority date where priority is claimed). The application may be published earlier if requested by the applicant; some confidential applications may be excluded from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request earlier publication; confidentiality exceptions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is examined only when a request for examination is filed. Any person can request examination within 3 years (or 5 years for applications filed before March 1, 2017) from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination order follows sequence of requests for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start and purpose of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination is carried out in the order of requests for examination. The purpose is to ensure that the application and invention meet the requirements of the Patent Act (Article 46 or 62). The prime task of the examiner is to deal with substantive requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal requirements are not satisfied, the examiner may invite the applicant to correct formal deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grounds for rejection before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner intends to reject a patent application under any subparagraphs of Article 62, the examiner shall give the applicant a chance to submit arguments by notifying grounds for rejection prior to issuance of the decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice enables applicant to respond with arguments or amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and arguments by applicant in response to rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit arguments in response to an examiner's notice of rejection and may file amendments to the specification or drawings within the period designated in Article 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination should take into account such amendments and arguments on re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after applicant reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking into account any amendments or arguments made by the applicant in reply to the rejection, the examiner should examine the application again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up examination must consider applicant's responses fully before final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of a patent when no grounds to reject found
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner finds no grounds to reject a patent application, he/she decides to grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard decision to grant follows substantive clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officio amendment of obvious errors when granting
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a decision to grant a patent, an examiner may amend ex officio obvious errors in the specification, drawing(s), or abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall notify the applicant of the errors to be amended ex officio along with certified copy of the decision to grant; applicant can decide whether to accept the ex officio amendment by the time for paying patent registration fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to reject after considering replies
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner examines the application again taking account of any amendments or arguments and considers that the applicant fails to overcome the rejection, the examiner shall issue a decision to reject the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is requested, prior decisions may be deemed withdrawn; see reexamination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/request for reexamination timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend a specification or drawings to request reexamination within 30 days from receipt of certified copy of the decision to reject (or extension if statutory period extended). The reexamination request is not allowed where a decision to reject is issued after reexamination or where a notice of appeal is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is a request for reexamination, the prior decision to reject is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is made, the examiner shall take into consideration any amendment provided by the applicant and re-examine the application according to the general examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after reexamination, grounds for rejection remain, a decision to reject after reexamination shall be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of examiners: speed, accuracy, independence
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall proceed with the examination with speed and accuracy in accordance with the Patent Act and related provisions. An examiner shall examine independently based on legal and technical knowledge, provided opinions of supervising officials be taken into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work under direction/supervision of bureau director general, division head, or examination unit head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and assisted examination for new examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly appointed examiner (not more than 1 year in the job) shall participate in examination as an assistant examiner. After that period, the examiner shall service the examination jointly with other experienced examiner for additional 1 year. Periods may be shortened if certain requirements are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures mentoring and quality control for inexperienced examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for convergence technologies and multi-technical aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimed invention relates to convergence technologies mixed with several technical aspects, the primary examiner may consult other examiners in charge of relevant sub-technical classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner shall notify applicant of consultation, names of consulting examiners and reason; documents related to consultation are made under joint names while reporting mainly by primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for foreign-language prior art expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may consult with other examiners who have expertise in foreign languages (French, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, etc.) for better understanding of prior art documents written in such languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consultations to improve prior art comprehension and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation between examiners for related applications filed same date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more related patent applications (including utility models) with common or corresponding technical features are filed by the same applicants on the same date and assigned to different examiners, one examiner can consult with the other(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates consistent treatment of related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-general convened joint conference for difficult rule application
rubrics_metrics.description: If a director general acknowledges a need for consulting advice where application confronts difficulties in unified rule application and judgment in examination, he may convene a joint conference of more than three examiners for opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for complex or unclear rule-application questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of confidentiality for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: According to duty of confidentiality (Article 60 of the State Public Officials Act), the examiner shall carry out examination duties (including interviews, teleconsulting, etc.) with caution. Documents related to application and examination shall not be carried out except for prior art searches, digitization, or online remote performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No response shall be given to requests for expert opinion, testimony, or inquiry on contents of a patent application, examination, trial, retrial, pending matters, or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and continuation rules when examiner transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more examiners shall be designated for each IPC and a primary examiner designated. Where the examiner transfers after issuance of the first office action, the examiner in charge shall continue examination up to his/her final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Examination Support Division appoints primary examiner at request of bureau director general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule that remanded or reexamination applications stay with same examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: An application requested for reexamination or returned to the examiner after revocation of examiner's original decision to reject shall be examined by the very examiner unless there is a justifiable reason for change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revoked and returned more than twice, the rejecting examiner may be changed to another one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on serving same IPC consecutively
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as necessary for expertise and efficiency, an examiner shall not be in charge of the same IPC for 5 consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotation supports objectivity and distribution of workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion/conflict rules for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner who falls under subparagraphs of Article 148 of the Patent Act, or an examiner with less than 2 years' experience assigned to applications from his/her former employment, shall be excluded from the concerned examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an examiner may avoid relevant examination with permit from director general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-reason changes in examiner designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation may change for special reasons (e.g., in case of a double patent application, the examiner of the original application can be designated; where multiple relevant applications of the same applicant are assigned to different examiners, examiner responsible can be changed in consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change only where necessary to ensure coherent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of examiner for ex-officio reexamination/refusal to accept ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a patent application subject to ex-officio reexamination or to a reexamination resulted from refusal to accept ex-officio amendment, the patent examiner who allowed grant shall continuously perform the examination without any special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of handling after ex-officio actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal reporting obligations for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner allows a patent or rejects (except where no written arguments/amendment submitted in response to notice), or where final disposal was revoked/remanded, the examiner shall report to head of examination team/division and then to general director of examination bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of reportable matters includes decisions to reject/allow, refusal to enter amendment, invalidation dispositions, notices of grounds for rejection, decisions on reexamination, third office action regarding deficiencies, dismissal of expedited examination request, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting exemptions/delegations by examiner grade
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on examiner grade (examiner, junior examiner, senior examiner, chief examiner), reporting to head of examination unit may be exempted in specified cases (e.g., junior examiner notifying expedited exam decisions when requester is not applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grade determined by advancement deliberation committee; experience and required training determine grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and name of authority for examination-related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If KIPO determines a due form for certain documents, it is principle to use it; if no due form, a general document form should be used. Attached documents shall be listed at end of document body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent examination shall be conducted in the name of the examiner in charge except for certain matters (Article 46 amendments, invalidation measures, returns per Article 11 Enforcement Rules, expedited examination matters); joint examinations use joint names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for accurate patent classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent classification assignment must be made accurately based on technical subject-matter of the invention to make search and access to patent documents easier by classifying technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate classification aids prior art search for examiners and public users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification flow (preliminary assignment, confirmation, correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow: Reception of application & formality check → Request for classification → Preliminary assignment → Confirmation of patent classification → Request for correction of classification → Approval/Refusal → Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized classification organization and Patent Examination Policy Division coordinate classification requests and allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-classification review and correction by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-classification of ordinary applications is conducted by a specialized classification organization; an examiner shall review whether the technical subject-matter of the claimed invention is classified appropriately pursuant to CPC/IPC and whether application is within scope of his/her classification before examination to confirm classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inappropriate, the examiner should apply for correction, request reallocation, or ask Policy Division to correct classification and reallocate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different confirmation process for national defence and PCT applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to national defense and PCT international applications have a different method to confirm classification than ordinary applications: confirmation by checking pre-classification on screen; PCT international applications are excluded from re-designation of pre-classification and subsequent processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner reviews pre-classification and either confirms or returns with suggested classification symbol and opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of classification during examination and grounds required
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is necessary to correct classification for accurate classification according to technical contents understood during examination, Correction of classification shall be applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for correction (related claims, references, etc.) shall be stated; Patent Examination Policy Division finally accepts or rejects correction after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for determining technical subject-matter for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of technical contents of an application, classification place among section, class, sub-class, main group, and sub-group shall be determined. The technical subject-matter is determined based on matters in claims in light of description and drawings. If claim unclear or delayed, the description or drawings determine technical subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is based on essential contents of claimed invention as a whole rather than formality like category of invention (example: electronic radio circuit classified as whole circuit unless core concerns specific part). If claims differ from description, description/drawings are additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main vs sub-classification when multiple technical subject-matters present
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple technical subject-matters are involved, core technical subject-matter representing the claimed invention as a whole is categorized as 'main classification', while other technical subject-matters are categorized as 'sub-classification'. If difficult to separate, classification sign of technical subject-matter in claim 1 can be referred as main classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claim 1 as tie-breaker when core cannot be isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule of IPC assignment: function-oriented vs application-oriented places
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPC has two kinds of classification places: 'function-oriented' and 'application-oriented'. For use inventions, if an appropriate application place exists it becomes classification basis; if none, function-oriented place becomes main classification and similar use place becomes sub-classification. For function-oriented inventions, classify based on function place; if IPC has no pertinent function place, use main use prescribed in specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple uses are mentioned, relevant function becomes classification; if multiple uses only extend main use, main use is main classification and others sub-classification (example: valves classified by function or by use classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and ordering of IPC entries in patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Three entries for IPC indicated in patent documents: 'IPC identification abbreviation', 'classification symbols or indexing code', and 'version'. Classification symbols and indexing code shall be indicated in order: invention information → additional information → indexing code. Invention information in boldface, additional in regular type; some countries use italic for extension level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing code used only for additional information; examples provided for style and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional information and indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information complements invention information and can be given by indexing code or classification symbols. Indexing code is designated based on indexing classification table categorized by technical functions (purpose, use, structure, material, manufacturing process, disposal process, control measure, etc.) not included in classification place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After designating classification symbol, code is designated for technical subject-matter useful to search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to state confidentiality due to national security
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention described in specification is required to be confidential due to national security, such requirement shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part VII, chapter 3 for more details on confidential handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification approach for divisional/converted/priority/related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to divisional application, converted application, domestic priority claim application, treaty priority claim application or application of lawful holder of the right, classification of the original application shall be identified first. Except when classifications of original obviously fail to correspond to later-filed application, it is preferable to remain the same classification of original application as main classification while designate newly granted classification as sub-classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves consistency across related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC assignment rule for apparatus vs method (fallback order)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, classification place for either an apparatus or a method shall be used if a pertinent place for either exists. If apparatus has no classification place, method in apparatus shall be used; if method has no place, place for apparatus which performs the method shall be used. If neither exists, place for product manufactured with apparatus or method shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides fallback order to select most appropriate classification place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products classification fallback
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufactured product shall be classified with place pertinent to the product. If no such place exists, use an appropriate function-oriented place; if none, classify based on use of the manufactured product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order: product → function → use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of multistage processes or plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A multistage process or a plant consisting of plural stages or composition with plural apparatuses shall be classified with the place pertinent to the composition. If no such classification place exists, the place for the output produced from the composition shall be used. Where constituents have individual characteristics, each constituent shall be classified too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composition has no intrinsic characteristics but constituents do, composition shall not be classified (i.e., classify constituents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of specific/structural parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural or functional specifics or parts in the claimed invention are used only for a certain apparatus, the claimed invention shall be classified into the place for the apparatus. However, if such specifics or parts can be used for more than 2 apparatus, it is advisable to classify into the place for those specifics or parts. Where there is no place for them, classify in place for the relevant apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose classification reflecting reusability and generality of the part.
